test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 09 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: __________ is an industry association and self-regulatory organisation (SRO) whose primary objective is to work towards the robust development of the microfinance sector.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Microfinance Institutions Network**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN) is an industry association that represents the microfinance industry in India.
 
• It is a self-regulatory organization (SRO) recognized by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
• The primary objective of MFIN is to work towards the robust development of the microfinance sector by promoting responsible lending practices and ensuring client protection.
 
• MFIN also works on policy advocacy, capacity building, and facilitating knowledge sharing among its members.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-help Group Association**

 
 
• Self-help groups (SHGs) are small voluntary associations of people, typically women, who come together to form a group for the purpose of savings and credit.
 
• SHGs promote savings among members and use the pooled resources to provide small loans to members.
 
• They play a crucial role in financial inclusion and empowerment of marginalized communities, especially women.
 
 
 
• **Microfinance and Investments Regulatory Authority**
 
 
• There is no known regulatory authority by this name specifically for microfinance and investments in India.
 
• Microfinance institutions in India are primarily regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
 
 
• **NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)**
 
 
• NABARD is an apex development bank in India, established to provide and regulate credit and other facilities for the promotion and development of agriculture, small-scale industries, cottage and village industries, handicrafts, and other rural crafts.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in the development of the rural sector in India.
 
• While NABARD supports microfinance activities, it is not an industry association or SRO specifically for the microfinance sector.
